question: In 2 Timothy 1:2, how does Paul affectionately address Timothy in his opening apostolic greeting?
opt1: To Timothy, my dearly beloved son
opt2: To Timothy, a fellow elder of Ephesus
opt3: To Timothy, an honorable scribe of the law
opt4: To Timothy, a companion in civic affairs
correct: To Timothy, my dearly beloved son
explanation: Paul conveys his profound personal love for Timothy, addressing him as his dearly beloved spiritual son. 2 Timothy 1:2 (KJV) - "To Timothy, my dearly beloved son: Grace, mercy, and peace, from God the Father and Christ Jesus our Lord."

question: According to 2 Timothy 1:5, what godly heritage and unfeigned faith dwelt first in Timothy's maternal family?
opt1: Which dwelt first in thy father Philip, and thy brother Titus
opt2: Which dwelt first in thy grandmother Lois, and thy mother Eunice
opt3: Which dwelt first in thy grandfather Simeon, and thy aunt Martha
opt4: Which dwelt first in thy mother Salome, and thy sister Lydia
correct: Which dwelt first in thy grandmother Lois, and thy mother Eunice
explanation: Paul commends the genuine generational faith that flourished in Timothy's grandmother Lois and mother Eunice before taking root in him. 2 Timothy 1:5 (KJV) - "When I call to remembrance the unfeigned faith that is in thee, which dwelt first in thy grandmother Lois, and thy mother Eunice; and I am persuaded that in thee also."

question: In 2 Timothy 1:6, what does Paul remind Timothy to do concerning the spiritual gift bestowed upon him?
opt1: That thou return the monetary gift sent from the church at Philippi
opt2: That thou surrender the priestly robe presented by the Ephesian elders
opt3: That thou stir up the gift of God, which is in thee by the putting on of my hands
opt4: That thou conceal thy prophetic calling until persecution ceases
correct: That thou stir up the gift of God, which is in thee by the putting on of my hands
explanation: Timothy is charged to rekindle and actively fan into flame the spiritual gift imparted at his apostolic ordination. 2 Timothy 1:6 (KJV) - "Wherefore I put thee in remembrance that thou stir up the gift of God, which is in thee by the putting on of my hands."

question: According to 2 Timothy 1:7, what spirit has God NOT given believers, and what threefold spirit has He imparted instead?
opt1: Not given us the spirit of wisdom; but of wealth, of pride, and of worldly dominion
opt2: Not given us the spirit of joy; but of sorrow, of fasting, and of legal penance
opt3: Not given us the spirit of liberty; but of servitude, of fear, and of ceremonial bondage
opt4: Not given us the spirit of fear; but of power, and of love, and of a sound mind
correct: Not given us the spirit of fear; but of power, and of love, and of a sound mind
explanation: God liberates believers from paralyzing fear, granting instead supernatural dynamic power, self-giving love, and disciplined mental soundness. 2 Timothy 1:7 (KJV) - "For God hath not given us the spirit of fear; but of power, and of love, and of a sound mind."

question: In 2 Timothy 1:8, what does Paul command Timothy not to be ashamed of, and what does he urge him to partake in?
opt1: Be not thou therefore ashamed of the testimony of our Lord, nor of me his prisoner: but be thou partaker of the afflictions of the gospel
opt2: Be not ashamed of thy Greek lineage, nor of thy youth: but be thou a contender in public rhetoric
opt3: Be not ashamed of thy poverty, nor of thy manual labor: but be thou a merchant of earthly goods
opt4: Be not ashamed of Roman citizenship, nor of imperial decrees: but be thou an advocate in civil courts
correct: Be not thou therefore ashamed of the testimony of our Lord, nor of me his prisoner: but be thou partaker of the afflictions of the gospel
explanation: Timothy is challenged to display unashamed boldness regarding Christ and Paul's imprisonment, willingly sharing in gospel suffering through God's power. 2 Timothy 1:8 (KJV) - "Be not thou therefore ashamed of the testimony of our Lord, nor of me his prisoner: but be thou partaker of the afflictions of the gospel according to the power of God;"

question: According to 2 Timothy 1:9-10, upon what basis were believers saved and called, and what did our Saviour Jesus Christ accomplish through the gospel?
opt1: According to our moral merit and Levitical sacrifices; Jesus Christ hath established an earthly political dynasty in Jerusalem
opt2: Not according to our works, but according to his own purpose and grace; Jesus Christ hath abolished death, and hath brought life and immortality to light
opt3: According to ancestral pedigree and philosophical wisdom; Jesus Christ hath secured exemptions from Roman imperial taxation
opt4: According to human vows and ascetic fasts; Jesus Christ hath rebuilt the earthly tabernacle of Moses
correct: Not according to our works, but according to his own purpose and grace; Jesus Christ hath abolished death, and hath brought life and immortality to light
explanation: Salvation originates in God's eternal sovereign purpose and grace before time began, manifested in Christ who defeated death and illuminated eternal life. 2 Timothy 1:9-10 (KJV) - "Who hath saved us, and called us with an holy calling, not according to our works, but according to his own purpose and grace, which was given us in Christ Jesus before the world began, But is now made manifest by the appearing of our Saviour Jesus Christ, who hath abolished death, and hath brought life and immortality to light through the gospel:"

question: In 2 Timothy 1:12, what triumphant confession of personal faith does Paul make despite his suffering and imprisonment?
opt1: For I know the strength of Roman law, and am confident that the emperor will exonerate my appeals
opt2: For I know the secret wisdom of Greek philosophers, and am persuaded that human reason cannot perish
opt3: For I know whom I have believed, and am persuaded that he is able to keep that which I have committed unto him against that day
opt4: For I know the power of earthly armies, and am convinced that Jerusalem will conquer all empires
correct: For I know whom I have believed, and am persuaded that he is able to keep that which I have committed unto him against that day
explanation: Paul's serene assurance amid suffering rests on his intimate personal knowledge of the faithful Redeemer who safeguards his eternal soul. 2 Timothy 1:12 (KJV) - "For the which cause I also suffer these things: nevertheless I am not ashamed: for I know whom I have believed, and am persuaded that he is able to keep that which I have committed unto him against that day."

question: What steadfast instruction does Paul give to Timothy in 2 Timothy 1:13 regarding apostolic teaching?
opt1: Revise the theological terminology of the apostles to conform to fashionable Athenian philosophy
opt2: Surrender sound doctrine whenever Roman civil magistrates threaten church assemblies
opt3: Debate speculative genealogical genealogies with anyone who questions church traditions
opt4: Hold fast the form of sound words, which thou hast heard of me, in faith and love which is in Christ Jesus
correct: Hold fast the form of sound words, which thou hast heard of me, in faith and love which is in Christ Jesus
explanation: Timothy is commanded to preserve unchanged the doctrinal pattern of sound words delivered by Paul, anchored in faith and love in Christ. 2 Timothy 1:13 (KJV) - "Hold fast the form of sound words, which thou hast heard of me, in faith and love which is in Christ Jesus."

question: In 2 Timothy 1:15, what painful desertion does Paul recount to Timothy concerning believers in Asia?
opt1: All they which are in Asia be turned away from me; of whom are Phygellus and Hermogenes
opt2: The churches of Macedonia refused to send letters of encouragement; of whom are Jason and Aristarchus
opt3: The elders of Corinth expelled Paul's representatives; of whom are Crispus and Gaius
opt4: The believers in Rome denied fellowship to Luke; of whom are Linus and Pudens
correct: All they which are in Asia be turned away from me; of whom are Phygellus and Hermogenes
explanation: Paul grieves over widespread desertion by former associates from the province of Asia, explicitly naming Phygellus and Hermogenes. 2 Timothy 1:15 (KJV) - "This thou knowest, that all they which are in Asia be turned away from me; of whom are Phygellus and Hermogenes."

question: In contrast to those who deserted Paul, what refreshing faithfulness did Onesiphorus show toward him according to 2 Timothy 1:16-17?
opt1: He sent monetary gold to pay Paul's legal fines, but avoided visiting him in prison
opt2: He oft refreshed me, and was not ashamed of my chain: but, when he was in Rome, he sought me out very diligently, and found me
opt3: He petitioned the Roman Senate for Paul's release, but remained in Ephesus
opt4: He composed philosophical treatises in defense of Christianity, but feared Paul's bonds
correct: He oft refreshed me, and was not ashamed of my chain: but, when he was in Rome, he sought me out very diligently, and found me
explanation: Onesiphorus proved fearless and sacrificial, searching Rome diligently until finding the imprisoned apostle and bringing him constant comfort. 2 Timothy 1:16-17 (KJV) - "The Lord give mercy unto the house of Onesiphorus; for he oft refreshed me, and was not ashamed of my chain: But, when he was in Rome, he sought me out very diligently, and found me."

question: According to 2 Timothy 2:2, what four-generation principle of disciple-making and leadership succession does Paul command?
opt1: The doctrines which thou hast studied in Greek schools, publish in public market scrolls for all passersby
opt2: The secrets which thou hast received in private visions, conceal inside subterranean caves for future generations
opt3: The things that thou hast heard of me among many witnesses, the same commit thou to faithful men, who shall be able to teach others also
opt4: The traditions of the Pharisees, enforce through municipal lawsuits upon all citizens
correct: The things that thou hast heard of me among many witnesses, the same commit thou to faithful men, who shall be able to teach others also
explanation: Paul establishes the enduring pipeline of spiritual succession: Paul to Timothy, Timothy to faithful men, and faithful men to others also. 2 Timothy 2:2 (KJV) - "And the things that thou hast heard of me among many witnesses, the same commit thou to faithful men, who shall be able to teach others also."

question: In 2 Timothy 2:3-4, what military imagery does Paul use to describe the single-minded focus of a Christian minister?
opt1: Accumulate earthly plunder, as a conquering mercenary; for worldly wealth proves superior military strategy
opt2: Enlist in Roman imperial legions; that political alliances may shield church gatherings from civil arrest
opt3: Retreat from all conflict into secluded deserts; for physical hardship contradicts divine blessing
opt4: Endure hardness, as a good soldier of Jesus Christ. No man that warreth entangleth himself with the affairs of this life; that he may please him who hath chosen him
correct: Endure hardness, as a good soldier of Jesus Christ. No man that warreth entangleth himself with the affairs of this life; that he may please him who hath chosen him
explanation: A minister must willingly endure hardship like a dedicated soldier, avoiding civilian entanglements to please his commanding Lord. 2 Timothy 2:3-4 (KJV) - "Thou therefore endure hardness, as a good soldier of Jesus Christ. No man that warreth entangleth himself with the affairs of this life; that he may please him who hath chosen him to be a soldier."

question: What rules govern the athlete and the farmer according to the metaphors Paul employs in 2 Timothy 2:5-6?
opt1: If a man strive for masteries, yet is he not crowned, except he strive lawfully; the husbandman that laboureth must be first partaker of the fruits
opt2: An athlete is crowned according to his physical strength, regardless of rules; while the farmer must sell his entire harvest to the temple
opt3: An athlete receives the prize through cunning deception; while the farmer must fast until the harvest is consumed by strangers
opt4: An athlete is crowned only if he defeats Roman gladiators; while the farmer is forbidden from tasting his own crops
correct: If a man strive for masteries, yet is he not crowned, except he strive lawfully; the husbandman that laboureth must be first partaker of the fruits
explanation: The Christian worker must obey divine rules like an athlete competing lawfully and display hard labor like an industrious farmer entitled to the harvest. 2 Timothy 2:5-6 (KJV) - "And if a man also strive for masteries, yet is he not crowned, except he strive lawfully. The husbandman that laboureth must be first partaker of the fruits."

question: In 2 Timothy 2:9, what glorious paradox does Paul proclaim regarding his personal bonds and the proclamation of the gospel?
opt1: Wherein I enjoy complete imperial liberty; but the word of God is restricted to the province of Asia
opt2: Wherein I suffer trouble, as an evil doer, even unto bonds; but the word of God is not bound
opt3: Wherein I am imprisoned in luxury; but the word of God is silenced by Roman magistrates
opt4: Wherein I am acquitted by the emperor; but the word of God has lost its supernatural power
correct: Wherein I suffer trouble, as an evil doer, even unto bonds; but the word of God is not bound
explanation: Though human heralds may be shackled as criminals in dungeon chains, the living Word of God remains untamed, free, and unstoppable. 2 Timothy 2:9 (KJV) - "Wherein I suffer trouble, as an evil doer, even unto bonds; but the word of God is not bound."

question: What faithful saying does Paul quote in 2 Timothy 2:11-13 regarding dying, suffering, denying, and believing in relation to Christ?
opt1: If we gain earthly wealth, we shall buy heavenly crowns: if we flee suffering, we shall rule nations: if we deny him, he will praise us
opt2: If we live in pleasure, we shall escape physical death: if we compromise with Rome, we shall be honored by angels
opt3: If we be dead with him, we shall also live with him: if we suffer, we shall also reign with him: if we deny him, he also will deny us: if we believe not, yet he abideth faithful: he cannot deny himself
opt4: If we observe Mosaic ceremonies, we shall attain immortality: if we break the sabbath, our souls shall vanish into nothingness
correct: If we be dead with him, we shall also live with him: if we suffer, we shall also reign with him: if we deny him, he also will deny us: if we believe not, yet he abideth faithful: he cannot deny himself
explanation: This early Christian hymn balances the glorious rewards of co-dying and co-suffering with Christ against the stern reality of denial, concluding with God's unalterable faithfulness. 2 Timothy 2:11-13 (KJV) - "It is a faithful saying: For if we be dead with him, we shall also live with him: If we suffer, we shall also reign with him: if we deny him, he also will deny us: If we believe not, yet he abideth faithful: he cannot deny himself."

question: According to 2 Timothy 2:15, what classic standard of biblical diligence is required of every minister before God?
opt1: Strive to obtain the applause of public crowds, an orator skilled in philosophical flattery
opt2: Labor to amass ecclesiastical treasures, a builder whose monuments impress Roman governors
opt3: Seek to enforce Levitical rituals, an inquisitor uncovering errors in civil tax records
opt4: Study to shew thyself approved unto God, a workman that needeth not to be ashamed, rightly dividing the word of truth
correct: Study to shew thyself approved unto God, a workman that needeth not to be ashamed, rightly dividing the word of truth
explanation: Believers are commanded to study Scripture rigorously and handle the message of truth accurately, standing unashamed under God's scrutiny. 2 Timothy 2:15 (KJV) - "Study to shew thyself approved unto God, a workman that needeth not to be ashamed, rightly dividing the word of truth."

question: In 2 Timothy 2:17-18, what heretical doctrine did Hymenaeus and Philetus spread, which ate like a canker (gangrene)?
opt1: Saying that the resurrection is past already; and overthrow the faith of some
opt2: Saying that Christ never physically rose from the dead, claiming His body was stolen
opt3: Saying that circumcision according to the law of Moses is mandatory for Gentile salvation
opt4: Saying that Emperor Nero is the prophesied Messiah who will rebuild Solomon's temple
correct: Saying that the resurrection is past already; and overthrow the faith of some
explanation: Hymenaeus and Philetus allegorized the resurrection as a purely past spiritual event, spreading destructive heresy that overturned the faith of some believers. 2 Timothy 2:17-18 (KJV) - "And their word will eat as doth a canker: of whom is Hymenaeus and Philetus; Who concerning the truth have erred, saying that the resurrection is past already; and overthrow the faith of some."

question: According to 2 Timothy 2:19, what two immutable inscriptions form the double seal upon the sure foundation of God?
opt1: The church shall conquer all earthly empires. And, Let every believer collect tithes from the nations
opt2: The Lord knoweth them that are his. And, Let every one that nameth the name of Christ depart from iniquity
opt3: The elect cannot experience physical suffering. And, Let all saints build monuments in Jerusalem
opt4: The law of Moses is eternal. And, Let every male convert receive physical circumcision
correct: The Lord knoweth them that are his. And, Let every one that nameth the name of Christ depart from iniquity
explanation: God's unshakable foundation bears two divine seals: divine sovereign knowledge of His own, and the moral obligation of believers to renounce sin. 2 Timothy 2:19 (KJV) - "Nevertheless the foundation of God standeth sure, having this seal, The Lord knoweth them that are his. And, Let every one that nameth the name of Christ depart from iniquity."

question: In the metaphor of the great house in 2 Timothy 2:20-21, how does a person become a vessel unto honor, meet for the Master's use?
opt1: If a man purchase vessels of gold and silver with temple offerings
opt2: If a man displays his wealth prominently before municipal magistrates
opt3: If a man therefore purge himself from these, he shall be a vessel unto honour, sanctified, and meet for the master's use, and prepared unto every good work
opt4: If a man isolates himself in physical wilderness seclusion away from all humans
correct: If a man therefore purge himself from these, he shall be a vessel unto honour, sanctified, and meet for the master's use, and prepared unto every good work
explanation: Cleansing oneself from dishonorable associations and doctrinal impurity sanctifies the believer for the Master's noble service in every good work. 2 Timothy 2:20-21 (KJV) - "But in a great house there are not only vessels of gold and of silver, but also of wood and of earth; and some to honour, and some to dishonour. If a man therefore purge himself from these, he shall be a vessel unto honour, sanctified, and meet for the master's use, and prepared unto every good work."

question: According to 2 Timothy 2:24-25, how must the servant of the Lord conduct himself when dealing with opponents of the gospel?
opt1: The servant of the Lord must argue aggressively in public squares, mocking the ignorance of his adversaries
opt2: The servant of the Lord must report theological opponents to Roman civil magistrates for execution
opt3: The servant of the Lord must impose financial penalties upon dissenters to compel outward compliance
opt4: The servant of the Lord must not strive; but be gentle unto all men, apt to teach, patient, in meekness instructing those that oppose themselves
correct: The servant of the Lord must not strive; but be gentle unto all men, apt to teach, patient, in meekness instructing those that oppose themselves
explanation: Pastoral apologetics demands gentleness, pedagogical skill, patience, and meekness, trusting God to grant opponents repentance leading to truth. 2 Timothy 2:24-25 (KJV) - "And the servant of the Lord must not strive; but be gentle unto all men, apt to teach, patient, In meekness instructing those that oppose themselves; if God peradventure will give them repentance to the acknowledging of the truth;"

question: According to 2 Timothy 3:1-2, what times will come in the last days, and what vices will characterize humanity?
opt1: Perilous times shall come. For men shall be lovers of their own selves, covetous, boasters, proud, blasphemers, disobedient to parents, unthankful, unholy
opt2: Glorious times of universal earthly prosperity shall come. For all men shall embrace the gospel without hesitation
opt3: Peaceful times of philosophical enlightenment shall come. For all nations will disband their armies
opt4: Times of strict legal obedience shall come. For all people will observe the ceremonial laws of Moses
correct: Perilous times shall come. For men shall be lovers of their own selves, covetous, boasters, proud, blasphemers, disobedient to parents, unthankful, unholy
explanation: Paul forewarns that the end times will be marked by severe moral degradation, characterized by rampant selfishness, arrogance, and irreverence. 2 Timothy 3:1-2 (KJV) - "This know also, that in the last days perilous times shall come. For men shall be lovers of their own selves, covetous, boasters, proud, blasphemers, disobedient to parents, unthankful, unholy,"

question: In 2 Timothy 3:4-5, what hypocritical religious condition does Paul identify, and what command does he issue concerning such people?
opt1: Lovers of fasting more than lovers of feasts; having angelic knowledge, but lacking earthly food: unto such give charity
opt2: Lovers of pleasures more than lovers of God; having a form of godliness, but denying the power thereof: from such turn away
opt3: Lovers of truth more than lovers of tradition; having Roman citizenship, but lacking church titles: unto such give leadership
opt4: Lovers of silence more than lovers of speech; having monastic vows, but lacking biblical scrolls: from such seek instruction
correct: Lovers of pleasures more than lovers of God; having a form of godliness, but denying the power thereof: from such turn away
explanation: Paul warns against religion that maintains hollow external rituals while repudiating genuine supernatural transformative power, commanding believers to separate from it. 2 Timothy 3:4-5 (KJV) - "Traitors, heady, highminded, lovers of pleasures more than lovers of God; Having a form of godliness, but denying the power thereof: from such turn away."

question: What tragic intellectual and spiritual futile loop describes those ensnared by false teachers in 2 Timothy 3:7?
opt1: Ever teaching, and having mastered all mysteries of Greek philosophy
opt2: Ever praying, and immediately receiving angelic revelations from heaven
opt3: Ever learning, and never able to come to the knowledge of the truth
opt4: Ever fasting, and having attained bodily sinlessness on earth
correct: Ever learning, and never able to come to the knowledge of the truth
explanation: They accumulate endless trivial information without ever arriving at saving, experiential knowledge of the gospel truth. 2 Timothy 3:7 (KJV) - "Ever learning, and never able to come to the knowledge of the truth."

question: In 2 Timothy 3:8-9, who are cited as historical examples of corrupt men who resisted the truth, and what will ultimately happen to their folly?
opt1: As Dathan and Abiram resisted Aaron, so do these seek the priesthood: they shall be swallowed alive in the wilderness
opt2: As Sanballat and Tobiah resisted Nehemiah, so do these oppose building: their walls will collapse into rubble
opt3: As Korah and his company offered strange fire, so do these preach false gods: their censers will be melted into bronze plates
opt4: Now as Jannes and Jambres withstood Moses, so do these also resist the truth: their folly shall be manifest unto all men
correct: Now as Jannes and Jambres withstood Moses, so do these also resist the truth: their folly shall be manifest unto all men
explanation: Just as Pharaoh's court magicians Jannes and Jambres opposed Moses only to have their impotence exposed, so end-time deceivers will have their folly unmasked. 2 Timothy 3:8-9 (KJV) - "Now as Jannes and Jambres withstood Moses, so do these also resist the truth: men of corrupt minds, reprobate concerning the faith. But they shall proceed no further: for their folly shall be manifest unto all men, as theirs also was."

question: In 2 Timothy 3:10-11, what cities does Paul recall where he suffered persecutions and afflictions, and what was the glorious outcome?
opt1: At Antioch, at Iconium, at Lystra; what persecutions I endured: but out of them all the Lord delivered me
opt2: At Alexandria, at Athens, at Rome; what debates I held: but by human philosophy I defeated them all
opt3: At Damascus, at Jerusalem, at Caesarea; what trials I faced: but the Roman Senate granted me immunity
opt4: At Philippi, at Thessalonica, at Corinth; what riches I gathered: but all of them I donated to the poor
correct: At Antioch, at Iconium, at Lystra; what persecutions I endured: but out of them all the Lord delivered me
explanation: Paul reminds Timothy of his historic missionary sufferings in Galatian cities, testifying that the Lord faithfully rescued him out of every trial. 2 Timothy 3:10-11 (KJV) - "But thou hast fully known my doctrine, manner of life, purpose, faith, longsuffering, charity, patience, Persecutions, afflictions, which came unto me at Antioch, at Iconium, at Lystra; what persecutions I endured: but out of them all the Lord delivered me."

question: What universal, unavoidable reality of the Christian life is declared in 2 Timothy 3:12?
opt1: Yea, and all that will live godly in Christ Jesus shall accumulate worldly wealth and earthly fame
opt2: Yea, and all that will live godly in Christ Jesus shall suffer persecution
opt3: Yea, and all that will live godly in Christ Jesus shall be granted diplomatic immunity by Roman law
opt4: Yea, and all that will live godly in Christ Jesus shall be spared from every earthly sorrow and sickness
correct: Yea, and all that will live godly in Christ Jesus shall suffer persecution
explanation: Faithful godly discipleship inevitably provokes friction and persecution from an unregenerate world system hostile to Christ. 2 Timothy 3:12 (KJV) - "Yea, and all that will live godly in Christ Jesus shall suffer persecution."

question: According to 2 Timothy 3:13, how will the moral trajectory of evil men and seducers develop as time advances?
opt1: Evil men and seducers shall gradually reform through civic education, embracing morality
opt2: Evil men and seducers shall vanish from the earth as human culture reaches enlightenment
opt3: Evil men and seducers shall wax worse and worse, deceiving, and being deceived
opt4: Evil men and seducers shall be compelled into repentance by imperial decree
correct: Evil men and seducers shall wax worse and worse, deceiving, and being deceived
explanation: Sin is degenerative: false teachers and corrupt men will sink deeper into spiritual depravity, simultaneously victimizing others and ensnaring themselves. 2 Timothy 3:13 (KJV) - "But evil men and seducers shall wax worse and worse, deceiving, and being deceived."

question: In 2 Timothy 3:14, what anchor does Paul urge Timothy to hold fast amid rising deception and apostasy?
opt1: Adopt new philosophical theories from visiting traveling teachers in Ephesus
opt2: Form political alliances with Roman magistrates to outlaw religious heresies
opt3: Abandon apostolic preaching to establish commercial trade guilds in Asia
opt4: Continue thou in the things which thou hast learned and hast been assured of, knowing of whom thou hast learned them
correct: Continue thou in the things which thou hast learned and hast been assured of, knowing of whom thou hast learned them
explanation: Timothy is exhorted to maintain unwavering constancy in apostolic doctrine, recalling the trusted character of those who taught him. 2 Timothy 3:14 (KJV) - "But continue thou in the things which thou hast learned and hast been assured of, knowing of whom thou hast learned them;"

question: According to 2 Timothy 3:15, what had Timothy known from his early childhood, and what spiritual power does it possess?
opt1: The holy scriptures, which are able to make thee wise unto salvation through faith which is in Christ Jesus
opt2: The legal traditions of Rome, which are able to secure civil citizenship and property rights
opt3: The mythological poems of Homer, which are able to teach classical eloquence in debate
opt4: The astronomical tables of Babylon, which are able to predict future earthly events
correct: The holy scriptures, which are able to make thee wise unto salvation through faith which is in Christ Jesus
explanation: Timothy's early immersion in Old Testament Scripture provided the divine foundation enabling saving faith in Christ Jesus. 2 Timothy 3:15 (KJV) - "And that from a child thou hast known the holy scriptures, which are able to make thee wise unto salvation through faith which is in Christ Jesus."

question: What classic, comprehensive doctrine of biblical inspiration and utility is declared in 2 Timothy 3:16-17?
opt1: Scripture contains occasional human inspirations, and is useful only for poetic contemplation and cultural literature
opt2: All scripture is given by inspiration of God, and is profitable for doctrine, for reproof, for correction, for instruction in righteousness: that the man of God may be perfect, throughly furnished unto all good works
opt3: Only the five books of Moses are inspired by God, while apostolic epistles represent fallible personal opinions
opt4: Scripture is inspired only when ratified by the Roman Senate, and is profitable solely for civil jurisprudence
correct: All scripture is given by inspiration of God, and is profitable for doctrine, for reproof, for correction, for instruction in righteousness: that the man of God may be perfect, throughly furnished unto all good works
explanation: Every portion of Scripture is divinely breathed (theopneustos), possessing complete sufficiency to instruct, reprove, correct, train, and thoroughly equip the servant of God. 2 Timothy 3:16-17 (KJV) - "All scripture is given by inspiration of God, and is profitable for doctrine, for reproof, for correction, for instruction in righteousness: That the man of God may be perfect, throughly furnished unto all good works."

question: In 2 Timothy 4:1-2, what solemn charge does Paul give Timothy before God and Christ Jesus, who shall judge the quick and the dead?
opt1: Build stone sanctuaries; collect imperial coins; appease pagan civic rulers with philosophical compromise
opt2: Retire from public ministry; write autobiographical chronicles; avoid preaching where persecution threatens
opt3: Preach the word; be instant in season, out of season; reprove, rebuke, exhort with all longsuffering and doctrine
opt4: Debate Roman lawyers; lobby the Senate for tax exemptions; enforce Mosaic circumcision on all citizens
correct: Preach the word; be instant in season, out of season; reprove, rebuke, exhort with all longsuffering and doctrine
explanation: Paul delivers an awe-inspiring final pastoral charge: proclaim God's Word urgently in all seasons, rebuking, correcting, and encouraging with tireless patience and solid doctrine. 2 Timothy 4:1-2 (KJV) - "I charge thee therefore before God, and the Lord Jesus Christ, who shall judge the quick and the dead at his appearing and his kingdom; Preach the word; be instant in season, out of season; reprove, rebuke, exhort with all longsuffering and doctrine."

question: According to 2 Timothy 4:3-4, what consumer-driven spiritual corruption will characterize audiences in the future?
opt1: They will demand deeper study of biblical Hebrew and refuse all Greek translations of Scripture
opt2: They will donate all their earthly property to the poor and live in total silence in the wilderness
opt3: They will enforce strict adherence to apostolic epistles and execute anyone promoting myths
opt4: They will not endure sound doctrine; but after their own lusts shall they heap to themselves teachers, having itching ears; and they shall turn away their ears from the truth, and shall be turned unto fables
correct: They will not endure sound doctrine; but after their own lusts shall they heap to themselves teachers, having itching ears; and they shall turn away their ears from the truth, and shall be turned unto fables
explanation: Audiences will reject uncompromised truth in favor of teachers who flatter their desires and tickle their ears with entertaining myths. 2 Timothy 4:3-4 (KJV) - "For the time will come when they will not endure sound doctrine; but after their own lusts shall they heap to themselves teachers, having itching ears; And they shall turn away their ears from the truth, and shall be turned unto fables."

question: In contrast to those who turn to fables, what fourfold ministerial duty is charged to Timothy in 2 Timothy 4:5?
opt1: Watch thou in all things, endure afflictions, do the work of an evangelist, make full proof of thy ministry
opt2: Pursue political titles, avoid all trials, do the work of a magistrate, build monuments in Ephesus
opt3: Withdraw from society, practice solitary fasting, do the work of a scribe, collect civic taxes
opt4: Seek popularity among crowds, flatter philosophers, do the work of a politician, avoid public debate
correct: Watch thou in all things, endure afflictions, do the work of an evangelist, make full proof of thy ministry
explanation: Timothy is commanded to maintain spiritual alertness, bear hardship bravely, evangelize lost souls, and fulfill every dimension of his calling. 2 Timothy 4:5 (KJV) - "But watch thou in all things, endure afflictions, do the work of an evangelist, make full proof of thy ministry."

question: What triumphant final testimony of his life and impending martyrdom does Paul proclaim in 2 Timothy 4:6-7?
opt1: For I am now expecting an imperial pardon from Nero, and my release is secured. I have purchased estates, I have built cities

question: According to 2 Timothy 4:8, what glorious prize awaits Paul, and to whom else will the Lord, the righteous Judge, award it?

opt3: A crown of righteousness, which the Lord, the righteous judge, shall give me at that day: and not to me only, but unto all them also that love his appearing
opt4: A silver monument erected in Jerusalem to commemorate the pioneers of the church

question: In 2 Timothy 4:10, what tragic departure of a former co-worker does Paul record with grief?

question: According to 2 Timothy 4:11, who was the sole companion remaining physically with Paul in Rome, and whom was Timothy instructed to bring with him?
opt1: Only Luke is with me. Take Mark, and bring him with thee: for he is profitable to me for the ministry

opt4: Only Peter is with me. Take Barnabas, and bring him with thee: for he is an apostle

question: In 2 Timothy 4:13, what personal items left at Troas with Carpus does Paul ask Timothy to bring when he comes?

opt4: The imperial passport signed by Caesar, and the Greek scrolls of Homer
correct: The cloke that I left at Troas with Carpus, when thou comest, bring with thee, and the books, but especially the parchments

question: In 2 Timothy 4:14-15, who does Paul warn Timothy to beware of because he did the apostle much evil and withstood their words?

question: At Paul's first legal defense when all men forsook him, who stood with him and strengthened him according to 2 Timothy 4:16-17?

explanation: Though human companions abandoned him during his trial, the Lord stood at Paul's side, empowering him to proclaim the gospel before imperial dignitaries and delivering him from immediate peril. 2 Timothy 4:16-17 (KJV) - "At my first answer no man stood with me, but all men forsook me: I pray God that it may not be laid to their charge.
